title: 2026 Ohio U.S. Senate special election
description: Ohio’s 2026 special U.S. Senate election will fill the remainder of the term that opened when J.D. Vance resigned to become vice president in January 2025. Appointed Sen. Jon Husted (R), the former lieutenant governor tapped by Gov. Mike DeWine, is running for a full term against former three-term Sen. Sherrod Brown (D), who lost re-election in 2024 but is seeking a return to Washington. Ohio has trended increasingly Republican — Donald Trump carried it by 11 points in 2024, and the GOP controls every statewide office and both Senate seats — but Brown’s history of winning statewide in a reddening state makes the race closely watched. The contest will test whether a well-known Democrat can still prevail in Ohio or whether the state’s recent Republican dominance will hold.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race in the last 90 days as of 2026-05-08.

candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.summary: Jon Husted is a Republican U.S. senator from Ohio who began serving in January 2025 after being appointed to fill the vacancy left by Vice President J.D. Vance. He previously served as Ohio's lieutenant governor, secretary of state, speaker of the Ohio House of Representatives, and a state legislator. Husted is the Republican nominee in the 2026 special election to complete the remainder of the Senate term.

Economy.stance: Supports business growth, workforce training, and regulatory reform. His public agenda also emphasizes reducing benefits cliffs and giving states more flexibility in anti-poverty programs.

sources.title: Upward Mobility Act - Senator Jon Husted
Husted leads bill to reform welfare, eliminate benefits cliff and pave path for families to pursue economic opportunities
About - Senator Jon Husted

Climate/Energy.stance: Advocates an all-of-the-above approach to domestic energy that includes expanding oil, gas, and coal leasing. He has supported methane capture from coal mines and backed policies to increase energy production, including proposals to boost energy development and rural Ohio jobs by reducing regulatory or tax barriers that impede domestic energy production.

sources.title: Husted backs bill to expand energy production, support rural communities
Husted in Zanesville with Ohio oil and gas leaders
Husted backs bill to boost domestic energy production

Healthcare.stance: Supports expanding rural health care access, including federal funding for rural communities and veterans, and says competition and more efficient delivery can help lower costs.

sources.title: Husted announces $202 million for Ohio rural health care access
Husted leads bill to improve benefits and health care for veterans
We must deliver quality, affordable health care for rural families

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Supports safeguarding the Hyde Amendment to bar taxpayer funding for abortions, including in federal employee health plans and ACA subsidies. His stated position includes exceptions for rape, incest, or to save the life of the mother.

sources.title: Husted supports bill to prevent taxpayer-funded abortions by safeguarding Hyde Amendment

Immigration.stance: Supports stronger immigration enforcement and border security, including funding for ICE and DHS. He has also backed measures aimed at combating fentanyl trafficking and limiting interference with law-enforcement operations.

sources.title: Securing the border - Senator Jon Husted
Husted backs Senate framework to fund law enforcement, keep border secure

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Supports expanding concealed-carry rights for qualified law-enforcement officers through the LEOSA Reform Act, which would broaden where officers may carry concealed firearms and extend training-certification timelines.

sources.title: Husted backs bill to expand law-enforcement concealed-carry rights

Foreign Policy.stance: Supports bipartisan sanctions targeting foreign buyers of Russian oil to reduce revenue for Russia and increase pressure over the war in Ukraine, with exemptions for countries that assist Ukraine.

sources.title: Husted joins bipartisan Senate push to sanction Russian oil buyers

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Has emphasized protecting women, children, and the unborn, and his public record includes support for abortion restrictions. Public criticism of his LGBTQ record has focused on earlier positions in Ohio-era policy debates.

sources.title: About - Senator Jon Husted
JD Vance’s replacement Jon Husted has anti-LGBTQ+ history

Tech & AI.stance: Supports accelerating AI adoption in business, government, and education. He has backed bills to recruit AI talent for the federal workforce, expand AI use in classrooms, help small businesses use AI, and protect consumers from AI-driven scams.

sources.title: Husted joins bill to help small businesses utilize AI
Husted leads bill to integrate AI talent in federal workforce
Husted leads bill to integrate AI in classrooms, prepare American students
Husted leads bipartisan bicameral bill to protect Ohioans from AI-driven financial scams

Local Issues.stance: Focuses on infrastructure, broadband, water access, rural health care, and economic opportunity in southeastern Ohio. He has highlighted legislation on rural water response, upward mobility, and rural health funding as part of that agenda.

sources.title: Senator Husted unveils new legislation to tackle key issues in Southeastern Ohio
Upward Mobility Act - Senator Jon Husted
Husted leads effort to expand broadband access in rural Ohio

Election Policy.stance: Supports requiring photo ID to vote and other election-integrity measures. He has promoted nationwide photo-ID standards and argued that the rules make voting easy while making fraud harder.

sources.title: Husted bill to require photo ID to vote blocked from passage
Husted op-ed: Senate Republicans want to make it easy to vote and hard to cheat in America

Education.stance: Supports school choice, including Ohio’s EdChoice model, and has backed efforts to add AI literacy and career-technical training in schools. His campaign frames these policies as giving parents more control over education decisions.

sources.title: Giving parents the choice for their kids' education - Jon Husted
Setting our students up for success - Senator Jon Husted
How Sen. Jon Husted has backed Ohio school choice and religious education programs

candidates.voting_summary: As appointed Senator since January 2025, Husted has voted consistently with the Republican caucus. In the 119th Congress he voted Yea on the reconciliation bill (S.2), Yea on all judicial and executive nominations, and Nay on a Democratic amendment to limit legal settlements. His legislative record includes sponsoring a photo-ID voting bill and the Upward Mobility Act.
candidates.donor_summary: Raised $10.5 million in total receipts for the 2025–2026 cycle through April 15, 2026, including $6.1 million in contributions and $4.4 million in transfers from joint fundraising committees. In the 2024 cycle, OpenSecrets reports $1.8 million raised with top industries: Party Committees ($123,605), Lawyers/Law Firms ($52,500), Retail Sales ($48,000), and Automotive ($40,150). Also operates the JOBS OPPORTUNITY NOW leadership PAC.

candidates.name: Sherrod Brown
candidates.summary: Sherrod Brown is a former Democratic U.S. senator from Ohio who served from 2007 to 2025. He is running in Ohio’s 2026 special U.S. Senate election after advancing from the Democratic primary.

summary_sources.title: United States Senate special election in Ohio, 2026

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Brown supports abortion rights and reproductive freedom, including federal protections for abortion and contraception and opposition to bans and restrictions. He has also been endorsed by Planned Parenthood organizations and has backed reproductive-freedom legislation.

sources.title: Planned Parenthood Advocates of Ohio endorsement of Sherrod Brown 2026
Planned Parenthood Action Fund endorsement of Sherrod Brown 2026
Sherrod Brown Congressional Scorecard - Reproductive Freedom for All

Climate/Energy.stance: Brown has earned a 93% lifetime score from the League of Conservation Voters. He supported the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which funded Great Lakes restoration; the GROW Act for conservation; and has voted for clean energy investments while opposing efforts to roll back EPA emissions rules that would harm Ohio manufacturing jobs. His campaign emphasizes energy affordability, domestic manufacturing, and protecting Ohio jobs tied to the energy sector.

sources.title: LCV Action Fund Endorses Sherrod Brown for U.S. Senate
A new Sherrod Brown? Democrat runs from climate agenda - E&E News

Economy.stance: Brown emphasizes rebuilding domestic manufacturing, supporting workers’ bargaining power, and opposing offshoring and unfair trade deals. His campaign also highlights infrastructure investment, lower drug costs, and pro-union policies as part of its economic agenda.

sources.title: Sherrod Brown — Issues (campaign site)
Sherrod Brown Is Grinding It Out - The Atlantic

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Brown supports gun-safety measures such as universal background checks, closing loopholes, and community violence-prevention funding while saying he supports the rights of law-abiding gun owners. This reflects the position described on his campaign issues page.

sources.title: Sherrod Brown — Issues (campaign site)

Election Policy.stance: Brown has a long Senate record supporting voting access and election-administration measures and opposing efforts that would restrict voting rights. His campaign site does not spell out a separate election-policy plank, so this summary reflects his public legislative record and issue emphasis on protecting democracy and voting access.

sources.title: Senator Sherrod Brown — Congress.gov
See Sherrod Brown's Key Votes — Vote Smart

Immigration.stance: Brown’s campaign messaging emphasizes border security alongside protections for long-term residents and workers. Reporting also says he has called for stronger border enforcement while criticizing harsh treatment of immigrants and supporting protections for groups such as Haitians in Ohio.

sources.title: Sherrod Brown — Issues (campaign site)
Ohio senators, governor respond to calls from Brown to extend protections for Haitians
Dem Senate candidate Sherrod Brown claims he supports 'closing ...'

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Brown has supported civil-rights protections and LGBTQ+ equality, including federal anti-discrimination and marriage-equality measures. He has also been endorsed by the Human Rights Campaign PAC for his Senate campaign.

sources.title: HRC PAC Endorses Sherrod Brown for U.S. Senate (Dec. 19, 2025)

Education.stance: Brown supports public education funding and higher-education access, including federal support for K-12 schools and Pell Grants. His campaign and allied education groups have emphasized support for teachers and public schools.

sources.title: Ohio Federation of Teachers Endorses Sherrod Brown

Healthcare.stance: Brown supports preserving the Affordable Care Act, expanding affordable coverage, and lowering prescription drug costs. His campaign materials also emphasize insulin-cost relief and protecting coverage for people with preexisting conditions.

sources.title: Sherrod Brown — Issues (campaign site)
Sen. Brown touts insulin price cap, fight for lower drug costs - Toledo Blade

Local Issues.stance: Brown’s campaign emphasizes manufacturing jobs, infrastructure investment, workforce training, and lowering costs for Ohio families. It also highlights support for veterans, seniors, and policies aimed at keeping jobs and investment in Ohio.

sources.title: Sherrod Brown - Issues

Foreign Policy.stance: Brown has supported U.S. aid to Ukraine, backing NATO allies, and sanctions on Russian aggression. His Senate record also includes support for bipartisan foreign-aid measures for U.S. partners.

sources.title: Senate passes Ukraine aid package with bipartisan support
Congress.gov bill text

Tech & AI.stance: As chair of the Senate Banking Committee, Brown held a hearing on AI in financial services in September 2023 and called for consumer and worker protections, including rigorous testing of AI models, privacy safeguards, and anti-discrimination measures. He has also said Washington must not repeat the mistakes made with Big Tech and social media when it comes to AI regulation.

candidates.name: Bill Redpath
candidates.summary: Bill Redpath is the Libertarian Party nominee in Ohio's 2026 special U.S. Senate election. A Perrysburg resident and former chair of the Libertarian National Committee (2006–2010), he has run for office nine times and is a 2016 inductee into the Libertarian Party's Hall of Liberty. His platform combines conservative economic positions (spending cuts, flat-tax reform, free trade) with liberal social stances (drug decriminalization, broad immigration, abortion rights).

summary_sources.title: About - Bill Redpath for U.S. Senate
What I Stand For - Anything that's Peaceful

Healthcare.stance: Redpath supports a free market in health insurance without mandated coverages, allowing insurance to be sold across state lines, and moving toward Health Savings Accounts for routine care with catastrophic insurance for major expenses. He opposes government-run healthcare and supports repealing the Affordable Care Act.

sources.title: William B. 'Bill' Redpath - iVoterGuide Questionnaire
Policies for the people - Vidette Online

Economy.stance: Redpath supports lower taxes, reduced federal spending, elimination of the Departments of Education and Housing & Urban Development, and replacing the current tax code with a flat-tax style reform plan.

sources.title: What I Stand For - Anything that's Peaceful
Bill Redpath for U.S. Senate

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Redpath supports an individual's right to access abortion, stating it should be allowed to save the life of the mother or if the fetus would be unable to feel pain. He agreed with the Supreme Court's decision overturning Roe v. Wade and opposes taxpayer funding for abortion providers.

sources.title: Get To Know Bill Redpath! - KMOV
William B. 'Bill' Redpath - iVoterGuide Questionnaire

Immigration.stance: Redpath supports very broad immigration, saying all immigration should be allowed except for a small set of people who are criminals, terrorists, seriously ill, or otherwise likely to harm others.

sources.title: What I Stand For - Anything that's Peaceful

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Redpath believes people convicted of violent crimes should not legally own or possess guns. He would consider other restrictions if they could be shown to enhance negative rights in society, but generally supports gun rights for law-abiding citizens.

sources.title: William B. 'Bill' Redpath - iVoterGuide Questionnaire

Foreign Policy.stance: Redpath says the United States should avoid war with Iran, seek congressional approval for military action, end the U.S. “special relationship” with Israel, and take a more restrained approach in the Middle East.

sources.title: What I Stand For - Anything that's Peaceful

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Redpath says he supports repealing federal laws on consensual crimes and restoring civil liberties, emphasizing that people should be free to live their own lives so long as they do not harm others or their property.

sources.title: Bill Redpath for U.S. Senate
What I Stand For - Anything that's Peaceful

Education.stance: Redpath calls for eliminating the U.S. Department of Education as part of reducing federal spending.

sources.title: What I Stand For - Anything that's Peaceful

Election Policy.stance: Redpath supports ranked-choice voting for single-winner elections, multi-member districts for the U.S. House under the Fair Representation Act, and the National Popular Vote compact for presidential elections.

sources.title: What I Stand For - Anything that's Peaceful

flags.concern: The stance summary cites an E&E News article titled 'A new Sherrod Brown? Democrat runs from climate agenda,' which carries a loaded framing suggesting Brown is retreating from climate commitments. While the source is cited, the stance description itself is neutral and balanced (mentioning his 93% LCV score, infrastructure support, and job-protection rationale). However, the inclusion of a source with a critical headline without explicit context that this is a critical framing could be misread as endorsing that framing. The actual stance text is fair.
flags.suggestion: Consider adding a brief note that the E&E News article presents a critical perspective, or rely more heavily on the LCV endorsement and Brown's own campaign messaging to lead the summary. Alternatively, this is acceptable as-is since the stance itself remains neutral.

flags.concern: The stance summary states 'Public criticism of his LGBTQ record has focused on earlier positions in Ohio-era policy debates' and cites an Advocate.com article titled 'JD Vance's replacement Jon Husted has anti-LGBTQ+ history.' This is sourced, but the phrasing 'anti-LGBTQ+ history' in the source title is a critical characterization. The stance itself remains factually neutral (describing his record without endorsing the criticism), so this is acceptable, but the reliance on a single advocacy-outlet source for a civil-rights stance (vs. multiple sources for other issues) is noted.
flags.suggestion: If additional sources on Husted's LGBTQ record are available (e.g., legislative votes, official statements), consider adding them for balance. Current sourcing is acceptable but thinner than other issues.

flags.concern: Gregory Levy's donor summary states 'No significant PAC or institutional contributions reported' and notes that 'totals appear negligible compared to major-party candidates.' This is accurate and appropriately contextualizes his grassroots fundraising model. No concern here; flagged only to note this is well-handled.

Bill Redpath's stance states he 'agreed with the Supreme Court's decision overturning Roe v. Wade and opposes taxpayer funding for abortion providers.' The source cited is an iVoterGuide questionnaire. This is a factual statement of his position, but the phrasing 'agreed with' is slightly more active/positive than a neutral 'supports' or 'backs.' However, this is a minor stylistic point and the stance is fundamentally neutral. No error flagged.

The summary states Husted 'began serving in January 2025 after being appointed to fill the vacancy left by Vice President J.D. Vance.' This is accurate per the sources cited. However, the summary does not mention that he is the 'incumbent' in the 2026 special election (though the profile correctly marks incumbent=true). This is a minor omission but worth noting for completeness.
flags.suggestion: Consider adding 'as the incumbent' or similar language to the summary to make his current status explicit, though the profile data structure already captures this.

flags.concern: Sherrod Brown's career_history shows he served as 'Ohio Secretary of State' from 1983–1991. My training data indicates Brown served as Ohio Secretary of State from 1983 to 1991, which matches the profile. However, the profile also states he 'Represented Ohio in the U.S. Senate for nearly two decades' (2007–2025), which is 18 years — accurate. No error detected; this is consistent with public records.

The voting_summary for Jon Husted states 'In the 119th Congress he voted Yea on the reconciliation bill (S.2), Yea on all judicial and executive nominations, and Nay on a Democratic amendment to limit legal settlements.' These are specific votes. The source cited is his voting record page (https://www.husted.senate.gov/legislation/voting-record/), which is his official Senate site. I cannot independently verify these specific votes from my training data (Husted was appointed in January 2025, after my knowledge cutoff for detailed voting records), but the source is authoritative. No error flagged; this is appropriately sourced.

The voting_summary for Sherrod Brown states he 'voted with the Democratic caucus over 90% of the time' and lists specific votes (Inflation Reduction Act, CHIPS Act, bipartisan infrastructure law, opposition to 2017 tax cuts, PRO Act, Butch Lewis Act). These are well-documented legislative positions. The source is GovTrack, which is authoritative. No error detected.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of Ohio's 2026 special Senate election with four candidates. Strengths: (1) All four candidates have detailed issue positions backed by credible sources (official campaign sites, FEC filings, news outlets, advocacy endorsements). (2) Career histories are documented and internally consistent. (3) Donor summaries are grounded in FEC and OpenSecrets data with specific dollar amounts and cycles. (4) Language is predominantly neutral across all candidates, with consistent framing of opposing positions (e.g., Husted's 'all-of-the-above energy' vs. Brown's 'clean energy investments' are both described factually without loaded adjectives). (5) The profile correctly distinguishes between high-confidence stances (backed by multiple sources) and lower-confidence gaps (e.g., Redpath and Levy on climate/tech, marked as 'no public position found'). Minor areas for improvement noted in flags below, but none rise to the level of factual error or systematic bias.

flags.concern: The career history field for Jon Husted is empty, despite the summary mentioning his extensive background as Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of State, and Speaker of the Ohio House.
flags.suggestion: Populate the career_history array with the roles mentioned in the summary to ensure consistency.

flags.concern: The career history entry for Sherrod Brown lists 'Ohio Secretary of State' from 1983-1991. My training data suggests he served as Ohio Secretary of State during this period, but the description says 'Held statewide office as Ohio secretary of state' while the title field is 'Ohio Secretary of State'. This is accurate, but the organization field says 'State of Ohio'—this is correct, but ensure the dates align with official records.

The stance is marked as 'No public position found'. Given the candidate's socialist platform, this is acceptable, but a search of the candidate's social media or specific party platform might yield a general stance on self-defense or gun control.
flags.suggestion: If no further information is found, the current 'No public position found' is appropriate and does not penalize the score.

Strong sourcing across all candidates and 12 issues with high-confidence citations from official campaign sites, FEC/OpenSecrets, Ballotpedia, GovTrack, and credible news outlets. forecast.rationale: This race looks highly competitive. The limited public polling from late 2025 through March 2026 shows a very tight contest, with Sherrod Brown holding small leads in the three most recent polls but Jon Husted leading in an earlier December poll; overall, the polling suggests no clear separation between the major candidates. Brown is a strong statewide Democratic figure with substantial fundraising and a history of outperforming his party in Ohio, which keeps Democrats very viable. But Ohio has trended strongly Republican in recent cycles, Donald Trump carried the state by 11 points in 2024, Republicans hold all statewide offices and both Senate seats, and Husted benefits from incumbency as the appointed senator plus the broader GOP state environment. With no public polling in the last 90 days and only a small set of polls overall, uncertainty is elevated. Given Brown’s demonstrated strength but Ohio’s recent Republican lean and Husted’s incumbency, Republicans have only a very slight edge.
